key_insight: A synthetic periodic large-scale structure introduced in the outer layer of a turbulent boundary layer causes phase-locked large-scale near-wall motions and modulates turbulence intensity through top-down interactions.
engineering_relevance: The study shows that outer-layer actuation can be used to probe and potentially control turbulent boundary-layer organization, with implications for drag reduction and flow management strategies.
method: Applied a plasma-based actuator in the outer region to generate a spanwise-uniform synthetic large-scale structure.
Measured the boundary-layer response using planar particle image velocimetry and spanwise-offset hot-wire probes.
Used phase-locked analysis to track downstream evolution of large-scale motions and turbulence amplitude modulation.
evidence_signal: Experimental data showed strong correlation between synthetic large-scale motions near the wall and periodic changes in turbulence amplitudes, with phase-dependent shifts in production and transport.
watch_item: The observed near-wall effects were intermittent and transient, so the influence of the synthetic structure may be limited in persistence and may not generalize to all turbulent boundary layers.
paper_title: Response of a Turbulent Boundary Layer to a Synthetic Periodic Large-Scale Structure
